sections.html:
DeKalb County fills Alabama's northeast corner against the Georgia line. Fort Payne is the seat and the largest city, and the other two cities are Henagar and Rainsville. Seventeen towns round out the list: Collinsville (partly in Cherokee County), Crossville, Fyffe, Geraldine, Hammondville, Ider, Kilpatrick, Lakeview, Mentone, Pine Ridge, Powell, Sand Rock, Shiloh, Sylvania and Valley Head. Sulphur Springs, Grove Oak, Dawson and Whiton are unincorporated. Plenty of residents commute to jobs in nearby counties.

Residents numbered 71,608 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 74,085 marks a 3.5 percent gain. There were 30,584 housing units and 27,145 households, with 11.2 percent of the units vacant. Owners hold 74.0 percent of occupied homes and renters 26.0 percent. About 88.3 percent of residents live in rural areas, so many houses sit on acreage and not on city lots. An empty house still carries a full tax bill each October.

A seller in a small town may deal with different utilities and code officers than one in Fort Payne, so make the town hall your first call.

Buyers look closely at older mountain houses, and the county has had events that explain why. An earthquake of magnitude 4.6 on April 29, 2003, centered near the county's eastern edge, cracked foundations and brought down a chimney. The April 27, 2011 Super Outbreak included the Rainsville tornado, rated EF5.

A house with older storm repairs, a cracked foundation or a patched roof can still sell, though it often takes a buyer willing to skip a long repair negotiation. Keep receipts and permits for repairs, and say plainly what was fixed and when. Problems that come out in an inspection hurt the price more than problems you disclosed first.

sections.h2: How Alabama classifies property for tax
sections.html:
Alabama sets assessment ratios by class, and the ratio decides what share of market value is taxed. The four classes apply statewide.

ClassType of propertyAssessment ratio
IUtilities30%
IIAll other property20%
IIIFarm, forest and owner-occupied10%
IVMotor vehicles15%

An owner-occupied house in DeKalb County falls in Class III at the lower ratio. A rental house falls in Class II, so a landlord's bill on the same market value runs higher. If you rent out a house you are selling, expect the buyer's tax picture to differ from yours.

sections.h2: Due dates and the delinquency timetable
sections.html:
October 1 is the due date, and a balance open past December 31 goes delinquent. From there the state calendar leads to a May tax sale.

  • October 1: due
  • January 1: delinquent
  • February: turned over to Probate Court
  • March: Probate Court meets
  • April: advertised for sale
  • May: tax sale

Phone the county Revenue Commissioner's office in Fort Payne to learn the exact payoff and when the office is open. Do this ahead of choosing a closing date. A written figure lets the title company match its own numbers.

Putting a deed on record costs a privilege tax of fifty cents per $500 of value, set by Alabama Code section 40-22-1, plus a separate recording fee at the probate office. The county gets one-third of the tax and the state two-thirds.

Either party must disclose the real price on a state revenue form. When no proof of price comes in, the tax may be figured on the latest assessment, and a penalty can follow.

Disagree with your valuation? The county Board of Equalization hears the challenge first, and circuit court is the next step if you lose. Under section 40-3-25 you have 30 days for that court appeal, and the tax keeps coming due while it is pending. Confirm the current rules with the Revenue Commissioner before you file.

sections.h2: Selling a house with tax problems
sections.html:
Rural acreage and older mountain houses bring their own difficulties.

  • An inherited house on land with several years of unpaid tax.
  • A rental assessed in Class II with a tenant who has left.
  • Storm or foundation damage that makes financing hard for a retail buyer.
  • A property on a private or mountain road that few agents want to show.

Because Alabama taxes follow the property, any unpaid balance usually comes out of the proceeds at closing. A cash buyer will take the house in its current state, settle the back taxes from the sale and close when you are ready.

  1. Request a payoff in writing from the Revenue Commissioner.
  2. Pull together the deed plus probate papers if you inherited.
  3. List road access or easement quirks for the title company.
  4. Weigh the offers and pick a closing date.

A road that is private or steep deserves a mention at the start. Tell any buyer who will do the maintenance and whether a written agreement exists, since lenders often ask.

Once you decide to sell, the steps are few. We discuss the house, where the taxes stand and what timeline suits you. Should you want an offer, we view the property and quote a figure. Accept it, and a title company opens a file, orders the search and requests payoffs. You sign, funds move, and the deed is recorded at the probate office.

The slowest part is usually paperwork, not price. Names on the deed need to match your identification. Every owner has to sign, so if the house passed to heirs, locate them early. A lien from an old loan or a contractor can appear in the search, and clearing it takes time, so ask the title company to run its search as soon as you have an offer in hand.

At the table, read the settlement statement. Taxes, any mortgage payoff and recording costs come off the top, and you receive the rest. Keep a copy with your tax records.

Because so many DeKalb houses are rural, land details can decide a sale. Know your acreage and where the lines run. If you have a survey, find it. If you do not, tell the buyer so, and expect the title company to ask whether a boundary has ever been disputed. A neighbor's fence, a creek or an old logging road can all blur a line.

Interstate 59 and U.S. 11 are the main routes, with state routes linking the smaller towns, and Norfolk Southern also runs through the county. A house near these is easier to reach and to show. One up a mountain road may need a four-wheel-drive visit, and agents often pass on it. That is one reason owners of such houses look at a direct sale.

Part of Little River Canyon National Preserve lies inside the county, and buyers who want land near it tend to ask about trails, water and access. Mention anything you know about springs, wells or septic systems, because rural buyers ask about them first.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of DeKalb County, Alabama?
faqs.a: Fort Payne is the county seat and the largest city.

faqs.q: What is the assessment ratio for a home in DeKalb County?
faqs.a: An owner-occupied home falls in Class III at 10 percent of value. Other property, including most rentals, is Class II at 20 percent.

faqs.q: When do DeKalb County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After December 31. The January 1 delinquency date is followed by a May tax sale.

faqs.q: How much is the deed recording tax in DeKalb County?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, plus the probate recording fee. The state keeps two-thirds and the county one-third.

faqs.q: Can I sell a DeKalb County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid balance is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, because Alabama taxes follow the property.
